exposure: preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) before 32 weeks
outcome: obstetric outcomes (placental abruption, cord prolapse, chorionamnionitis)
cohort: Pregnant women admitted for preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) before 32 weeks of gestation.
finding: Neonatal survival significantly improves with higher gestational age at PPROM, increasing by over 33% when PPROM occurs after 24 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: less than 32 weeks at PPROM, with categorization into < 24 weeks, 24 to 28 weeks, and 28 to 32 weeks.
